import random
import os
import struct

# Generator for an arbitrary byte string used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# Context: cairo_tag_begin attributes is a free-form string; any bytes allowed.
# We generate interesting, valid byte sequences covering:
# - Empty string
# - ASCII text with key=value pairs common to cairo tags (e.g., id, href, title)
# - UTF-8 and non-UTF-8 bytes
# - Long strings near typical thresholds
# - Strings with embedded NULs, whitespace, XML-like attrs, punctuation
# - Repeated patterns and random binary
# Size kept <= 4096 bytes

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"id", b"href", b"title", b"lang", b"class", b"dir",
    b"role", b"data-foo", b"data-bar", b"aria-label",
    b"x", b"y", b"width", b"height",
    b"color", b"font", b"weight", b"style", b"italic", b"bold",
]

ASCII_VALUES = [
    b"123", b"abc", b"/relative/path", b"https://example.com/", b"mailto:test@example.com",
    b"true", b"false", b"yes", b"no", b"none", b"auto",
    b"left", b"right", b"ltr", b"rtl",
]

UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    "Hello, 世界".encode("utf-8"),
    "été naïve café".encode("utf-8"),
    "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢".encode("utf-8"),
    "emoji: 😀🖼️✍️".encode("utf-8"),
]

# Some deliberately invalid UTF-8 byte sequences (still valid as free-form bytes)
INVALID_UTF8 = [
    b"\xC3",              # truncated 2-byte seq
    b"\xE2\x82",          # truncated 3-byte seq
    b"\xF0\x9F\x92",     # truncated 4-byte seq
    b"\x80\x80\x80",     # stray continuation bytes
]

PUNCT = b" \t\r\n,;:.!?'\"/\\()[]{}<>|@#$%^&*-+=_`~"

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _kv_attrs(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(count):
        k = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        # choose quote type
        quote = rng.choice([b'"', b"'"])
        v_base = rng.choice(ASCII_VALUES)
        # maybe add utf8 or punctuation
        tail = b""
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            tail += rng.choice(UTF8_SNIPPETS)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            tail += rng.choice([PUNCT, b"", b" "]) + (b";" if rng.random() < 0.3 else b"")
        v = v_base + tail
        # maybe escape quotes
        if quote == b'"':
            v = v.replace(b'"', b'"')
        else:
            v = v.replace(b"'", b"'")
        parts.append(k + b"=" + quote + v + quote)
    sep = rng.choice([b" ", b"\n", b"\t "])
    return sep.join(parts)


def _embed_nuls(rng: random.Random, data: bytes, max_nuls: int = 3) -> bytes:
    if not data:
        data = b" "
    b = bytearray(data)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, max_nuls)):
        pos = rng.randrange(0, len(b) + 1)
        b[pos:pos] = b"\x00"
    return bytes(b)


def _make_case(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(8)

    if choice == 0:
        # Empty or very small
        return b"" if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.choice([b" ", b"\n", b"\t"]) 

    if choice == 1:
        # Simple ASCII key=value list
        cnt = rng.randint(1, 8)
        return _kv_attrs(rng, cnt)

    if choice == 2:
        # XML-like attributes inside angle brackets style
        cnt = rng.randint(1, 10)
        attrs = _kv_attrs(rng, cnt)
        prefix = rng.choice([b"", b"class='c' ", b"data-x=1 "])
        return prefix + attrs

    if choice == 3:
        # UTF-8 rich text with punctuation
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
            parts.append(rng.choice(UTF8_SNIPPETS))
            parts.append(rng.choice([PUNCT, b" ", b"\n"]))
        return b"".join(parts)

    if choice == 4:
        # Include invalid UTF-8 mixed with valid
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
            parts.append(rng.choice(UTF8_SNIPPETS + INVALID_UTF8 + [b"="] + [PUNCT]))
        return b"".join(parts)

    if choice == 5:
        # Repeated pattern near thresholds
        base = rng.choice([b"id=\"a\" ", b"href='x' ", b"title=\"t\" "])
        repeat = rng.randint(32, 256)
        data = base * repeat
        # Clamp size
        return data[: min(len(data), MAX_SIZE)]

    if choice == 6:
        # Random binary blob with embedded NULs
        n = rng.randint(0, min(2048, MAX_SIZE))
        blob = _rand_bytes(rng, n)
        return _embed_nuls(rng, blob, max_nuls=5)

    # choice == 7
    # Mixed: key=val list + binary tail
    attrs = _kv_attrs(rng, rng.randint(2, 12))
    tail_len = rng.randint(0, 512)
    tail = _rand_bytes(rng, tail_len)
    out = attrs + b" " + tail
    return out[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose 1-3 segments to concatenate, to vary content while staying valid
    segments = []
    total_limit = MAX_SIZE
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        seg = _make_case(rng)
        # Ensure we don't exceed limit
        if len(seg) > total_limit:
            seg = seg[:total_limit]
        segments.append(seg)
        total_limit -= len(seg)
        if total_limit <= 0:
            break
    data = b" ".join(segments)
    # Final clamp
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data

# This generator targets Cairo stubs that consume UTF-8 strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# It returns a single bytes buffer that the fuzzing harness will split to serve
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls. We therefore pack several interesting UTF-8
# strings back-to-back, separated by NUL ("\x00"), so each call can read a
# distinct, valid string. We keep the content within 4096 bytes.
#
# Goals based on stubs:
# - Font family names for cairo_select_font_face and toy font creation: include
#   common families and edge cases (empty -> harness defaults to "sans").
# - Text strings for cairo_show_text, cairo_text_path, text_extents, and shaping
#   APIs: include diverse UTF-8 covering ASCII, accents, RTL, CJK, emoji,
#   combining marks, long strings, whitespace-only, punctuation, mixed scripts,
#   and numbers. All must be valid UTF-8 and NUL-terminated for each string.

COMMON_FAMILIES = [
    "sans", "serif", "monospace",
    "Helvetica", "Arial", "Times New Roman", "Courier New", "DejaVu Sans",
    "Noto Sans", "Noto Serif", "Noto Sans CJK JP", "Comic Sans MS",
    "Symbola", "Liberation Sans", "Liberation Serif", "Liberation Mono",
]

# Diverse valid UTF-8 samples
BASE_TEXT_SAMPLES = [
    "Hello, Cairo!",                          # ASCII
    "",                                       # empty (valid, some stubs accept it)
    "   ",                                   # spaces
    "\t\r\n",                               # control whitespace
    "Café naïve façade coöperate",          # Latin-1 accents
    "Αλφάβητο ελληνικά",                    # Greek
    "Привет мир",                            # Cyrillic
    "مرحبا بالعالم",                         # Arabic (RTL)
    "שלום עולם",                             # Hebrew (RTL)
    "こんにちは世界",                        # Japanese
    "你好，世界",                              # Chinese
    "안녕하세요 세계",                         # Korean
    "हैलो दुनिया",                           # Devanagari
    "😀😃😄😁😆😅😂🤣",                      # Emoji sequence

    "e bell",                 # low controls (valid bytes in UTF-8 for <0x80)
    "1234567890",                             # digits
    "!@#$%^&*()_-+=[]{}|;:'\",.<>/?`~",    # punctuation
    "Mixed عربى English 日本語 😀",           # mixed scripts
]

# Some longer paragraphs to exercise layout and clustering
LONG_SAMPLES = [
    "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.",
    "これは長めのテキストで、字形選択やクラスタリングの挙動を確認するために使われます。複数の文字種と句読点を含みます。",
    "هذا نص طويل نسبيًا لاختبار تحويل النص إلى محارف وقياسات الامتدادات، مع بعض التشكيل: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ",
]

# Reasonable toy font families beyond COMMON_FAMILIES for variety
MORE_FAMILIES = [
    "Times", "Courier", "Georgia", "Tahoma", "Verdana", "Ubuntu", "Cantarell",
    "Fira Sans", "Inter", "Source Sans Pro", "Source Serif Pro",
]

# Utility to make a moderately long random valid UTF-8 string from codepoint ranges
# while avoiding surrogates and noncharacters.
def rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Unicode ranges to sample from (BMP plus some astral for emoji-like)
    ranges = [
        (0x20, 0x7E),       # printable ASCII
        (0x00A0, 0x024F),   # Latin-1 supplement + extended
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
        (0x0590, 0x05FF),   # Hebrew
        (0x0600, 0x06FF),   # Arabic
        (0x0900, 0x097F),   # Devanagari
        (0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
        (0x30A0, 0x30FF),   # Katakana
        (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs
        (0xAC00, 0xD7A3),   # Hangul Syllables
        (0x1F600, 0x1F64F), # Emoticons
    ]
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        r = ranges[rng.randrange(len(ranges))]
        cp = rng.randrange(r[0], r[1] + 1)
        # skip surrogates and noncharacters
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            cp = 0xE000
        if (cp & 0xFFFF) in (0xFFFE, 0xFFFF):
            cp = 0xFFFD
        s.append(chr(cp))
    return "".join(s)

def build_strings(seed: int) -> List[str]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a selection of family names: guaranteed valid and common
    fams = []
    fams.extend(COMMON_FAMILIES)
    fams.extend(rng.sample(MORE_FAMILIES, k=min(5, len(MORE_FAMILIES))))

    # Include a few randomly generated family-like names (ASCII letters and spaces)
    for _ in range(3):
        n = rng.randint(3, 14)
        name = "".join(rng.choice("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz ") for _ in range(n)).strip()
        if not name:
            name = "Sans"
        fams.append(name)

    # Text samples pool
    texts = []
    texts.extend(BASE_TEXT_SAMPLES)
    texts.extend(LONG_SAMPLES)

    # Add random valid UTF-8 strings of various lengths to exercise shaping
    for ln in [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 55]:
        texts.append(rand_utf8(rng, ln))
    for _ in range(5):
        texts.append(rand_utf8(rng, rng.randint(60, 180)))

    # Mix in some repeated characters and combining marks sequences
    texts.append("e01" * 20)  # e + combining acute repeated
    texts.append("A" * 200)
    texts.append("😀" * 64)

    # Order the combined list with an interleaving of families and texts so that
    # successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls see varied content.
    out: List[str] = []

    # Start with a family to satisfy early font-face calls; then text, etc.
    fam_iter = iter(fams)
    txt_iter = iter(texts)

    # Interleave up to a reasonable count, leaving rest appended
    for _ in range(min(len(fams), len(texts))):
        try:
            out.append(next(fam_iter))
        except StopIteration:
            break
        try:
            out.append(next(txt_iter))
        except StopIteration:
            break

    # Append remaining
    out.extend(list(fam_iter))
    out.extend(list(txt_iter))

    # Ensure the very first few entries are strong defaults if consumed early
    # by multiple stubs
    out.insert(0, "sans")
    out.insert(1, "Hello world")

    return out


def pack_cstring_list(strings: List[str], max_bytes: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    # Pack as NUL-terminated UTF-8 cstrings back-to-back.
    buf = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        bs = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict') + b"\x00"
        if len(buf) + len(bs) > max_bytes:
            break
        buf += bs
    # Guarantee at least one NUL even if empty
    if not buf:
        buf = bytearray(b"\x00")
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    strings = build_strings(seed)
    return pack_cstring_list(strings, 4096)

# - Fill its malloc'ed buffer by repeating the bytes from FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
#
# Therefore, to maximize valid and interesting behavior, we craft FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# so that when repeated across the pixel buffer it contains plausible pixel patterns
# for all formats cairo may select. We include structured sequences and gradients
# that look meaningful under ARGB32/RGB24 as well as bit-patterns that exercise
# A8/A1 masks and unusual values for RGB16_565/RGB30/RGB96F/RGBA128F.
#
# The function returns bytes (<= 4096) as required.

MAX_OUT = 4096

# Utility to clamp and pack floats to IEEE-754 little-endian 32-bit

def f32(v: float) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<f', v)


def pack_rgb32(a: int, r: int, g: int, b: int) -> bytes:
    # ARGB32 in native-endian 32-bit. Cairo uses ARGB32 (premultiplied). We don't premultiply
    # here—cairo accepts arbitrary bytes, and premul vs non-premul is still valid input.
    # We'll emit in little endian as most platforms; bytes are order b,g,r,a in memory for LE
    val = ((a & 0xFF) << 24) | ((r & 0xFF) << 16) | ((g & 0xFF) << 8) | (b & 0xFF)
    return struct.pack('<I', val)


def pack_rgb24(r: int, g: int, b: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([b & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, r & 0xFF])


def pack_rgb565(r: int, g: int, b: int) -> bytes:
    # 5 bits R, 6 bits G, 5 bits B
    rv = (r & 0xFF) * 31 // 255
    gv = (g & 0xFF) * 63 // 255
    bv = (b & 0xFF) * 31 // 255
    v = (rv << 11) | (gv << 5) | bv
    return struct.pack('<H', v)


def pack_rgb30(r: int, g: int, b: int, a: int = 0xFF) -> bytes:
    # 10 bits per channel in a 32-bit word; Cairo RGB30 is generally xRGB30
    rv = (r & 0xFF) * 1023 // 255
    gv = (g & 0xFF) * 1023 // 255
    bv = (b & 0xFF) * 1023 // 255
    # layout: bbbbbbbbbbgGGGGGGGGGrRRRRRRRRR with 2 padding bits (implementation-defined).
    # We'll choose: [xx][R10][G10][B10] little-endian packing of 32-bit value.
    v = (rv << 20) | (gv << 10) | bv
    return struct.pack('<I', v)


def gen_palette() -> Tuple[Tuple[int,int,int,int], ...]:
    # Useful palette including extremes and alpha variants
    return (
        (0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00),  # fully transparent black
        (0xFF, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00),  # opaque black
        (0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF),  # opaque white
        (0x80, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00),  # 50% alpha red
        (0x80, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00),  # 50% alpha green
        (0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF),  # 50% alpha blue
        (0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00),  # red
        (0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00),  # green
        (0xFF, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF),  # blue
        (0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF),  # magenta
        (0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF),  # cyan
        (0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00),  # yellow
    )


def make_blocks(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    data = bytearray()

    # 1) ARGB32 blocks: solid colors, gradient lines, checkerboard
    palette = list(gen_palette())
    rnd.shuffle(palette)

    # solid colors
    for a, r, g, b in palette[:6]:
        data += pack_rgb32(a, r, g, b) * rnd.randint(4, 16)

    # horizontal gradient from black to white
    for i in range(32):
        v = int(i * 255 / 31)
        data += pack_rgb32(0xFF, v, v, v)

    # alpha ramp
    for i in range(32):
        a = int(i * 255 / 31)
        data += pack_rgb32(a, 0x80, 0x40, 0xC0)

    # 2) RGB24 blocks
    for r, g, b in [(255,0,0),(0,255,0),(0,0,255),(255,255,255),(0,0,0)]:
        data += pack_rgb24(r,g,b) * rnd.randint(8, 24)

    # 3) A8 blocks: alpha masks including edges and ramps
    a_vals = [0x00, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFE, 0xFF]
    for a in a_vals:
        data += bytes([a]) * rnd.randint(16, 64)
    # ramp
    data += bytes([int(i * 255 / 63) for i in range(64)])

    # 4) A1 bit masks: construct bytes with typical bit patterns
    patterns = [0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA, 0x0F, 0xF0, 0x33, 0xCC]
    for p in patterns:
        data += bytes([p]) * rnd.randint(8, 32)

    # 5) RGB16_565 blocks
    for r,g,b in [(255,0,0),(0,255,0),(0,0,255),(255,255,0),(0,255,255),(255,0,255),(128,128,128)]:
        data += pack_rgb565(r,g,b) * rnd.randint(8, 24)

    # 6) RGB30 blocks
    for r,g,b in [(255,0,0),(0,255,0),(0,0,255),(255,255,255),(0,0,0),(200,100,50)]:
        data += pack_rgb30(r,g,b) * rnd.randint(8, 24)

    # 7) RGB96F and RGBA128F float blocks: pack 0.0, 0.5, 1.0 and some randoms
    floats = [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, -0.5]
    # RGB96F (3 floats)
    for _ in range(16):
        r = rnd.choice(floats)
        g = rnd.choice(floats)
        b = rnd.choice(floats)
        data += f32(r) + f32(g) + f32(b)
    # RGBA128F (4 floats)
    for _ in range(16):
        r = rnd.choice(floats)
        g = rnd.choice(floats)
        b = rnd.choice(floats)
        a = rnd.choice(floats)
        data += f32(r) + f32(g) + f32(b) + f32(a)

    # Trim to MAX_OUT to respect size limit, but ensure non-empty
    if len(data) == 0:
        data = bytearray(b"\x00")
    if len(data) > MAX_OUT:
        data = data[:MAX_OUT]
    return bytes(data)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)
    return make_blocks(seed)
